entries.title: A distraction and a stolen meal
entries.odia:
ଅଇଲା ମାଳି, ମାଇଲା ତାଳି
ଧରି ପଳେଇଲା, ଖେଚୁଡ଼ି ଥାଳି।
entries.literal_meaning: Mali arrived, clapped, and ran away carrying the plate of khichdi.
entries.explanation: A show of activity diverts attention while someone takes the thing that matters. The rhyme exposes the trick rather than admiring the theft.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର କିମ୍ବା ହୋହଲ୍ଲାରେ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଧ୍ୟାନ ଅଟକାଇ ନିଜ ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥ ସାଧିବାର କୌଶଳକୁ ଏହି କଥା ଧରେ।
entries.usage_example: During a noisy discussion about small expenses, someone quietly takes the shared funds. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source supplies a deception gloss. ମାଳି is retained as the rhyme’s label; it is not evidence about a community’s conduct.

entries.title: A gift with little to give
entries.odia:
ଅଗସ୍ତି ଦେଲେ ଦାନ
କଷା ଗୁଆକୁ ପଚା ପାନ ।
entries.literal_meaning: Agasti gave a gift: astringent areca nut and rotten betel leaf.
entries.explanation: The announcement of generosity is undercut by the poor gift itself. This is an editorial reading of the contrast; the rhyme does not establish a historical donor or event.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦାନର ନାଁ ବଡ଼ ହେଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦିଆଯାଇଥିବା ଜିନିଷର କାମ ନ ଥାଇପାରେ। ଏଠାରେ ଦାନର ଘୋଷଣା ଓ ତାହାର ମାନ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ତଫାତ ଦିଶେ।
entries.usage_example: A celebrated equipment donation turns out to consist of unusable machines. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source gives no explanatory gloss. Agasti is not identified here with a verified person; no antiquity claim follows from the name.

entries.title: Three people, three ways
entries.odia:
ଅଗା, ବଗା, ଖଗା
ତିନିହେଁ ତିନି ଅଲଗା ।
entries.literal_meaning: Aga, Baga and Khaga: all three are different from one another.
entries.explanation: Being grouped together does not make people alike. The little series of names makes difference easy to remember; the particular disagreement depends on the occasion.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏକାଠି ଥିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ଭାବନା ଓ ଚାଲିଚଳନ ଏକ ହୁଏନାହିଁ। ତିନିଟି ନାଁରେ ସେହି ତଫାତକୁ ମନେ ରଖିବା ସହଜ ହୁଏ।
entries.usage_example: Three friends planning a journey each prefer a different destination. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: A literal, bounded editorial reading; the source supplies no origin story or named real individuals.

entries.cultural_context: The captured example supplies the money-seeking situation. This is an animal comparison, not a statement about human worth.

entries.title: Standing like a post
entries.explanation: Someone remains standing stiffly or motionlessly. In the source’s example, the speaker has already invited the person to sit; the comparison conveys impatience, not a diagnosis of the person’s motives.

entries.cultural_context: The source’s invitation-to-sit example supports this limited reading; no claim of laziness or incapacity is warranted.

entries.title: Good intentions, a spoiled result
entries.literal_meaning: While shaping a deity, one made a monkey.
entries.explanation: The intended improvement turns into a spoiled result. Good intentions alone do not guarantee that the work will turn out as planned.

entries.usage_example: An attempt to repair a small tear leaves a much larger hole. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source provides an explicit spoiled-work gloss and a synonymous expression. The image is not evidence of an actual sculptor or religious episode.

entries.title: A benefit out of reach
entries.literal_meaning: What does the crow gain when the bael fruit ripens?
entries.explanation: A desirable thing can become available without helping someone who cannot make use of it. The saying asks who actually benefits, not merely whether something is good.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭଲ ଜିନିଷ ମିଳିଲେ ବି ତାହାକୁ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ନ ପାରିଲେ ଲାଭ ମିଳେନାହିଁ। କାହା ପାଇଁ ଜିନିଷଟି ଉପଯୋଗୀ, ସେ କଥା ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ।
entries.usage_example: A village receives digital equipment but has no reliable electricity to use it. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source gloss concerns a useful thing failing to reach the appropriate person. The fruit-and-crow image is proverbial, not a biological claim about every crow.

entries.literal_meaning: Through the hand’s idleness, the moustache is crooked.

entries.usage_example: A worker notices an unstable stack and keeps others away until it is secured. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

entries.title: An old habit returns
entries.explanation: The source uses the curved tail as an image of a persistent disposition. In ordinary conversation it can express frustration when a habit returns; it does not prove that people are incapable of change.

entries.title: Frightened by another’s trouble
entries.odia:
ବିରି ମାଡ଼ ଶୁଣି କୋଳଥ ଚୋପା
ହରଡ଼ କହୁଛି ରଖଲୋ ବାପା ॥
entries.literal_meaning: Hearing the black gram being beaten, horse-gram husk; the pigeon pea says, “Save me, father.”
entries.explanation: The source explains the fear that spreads when someone sees another in trouble. The pulses speak as if the next blow might reach them too.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ବିପଦ ପଡ଼ିବା ଦେଖି ନିଜେ ଭୟ ପାଇବାର କଥା ଏହା। ନିଜ ପାଳି ଆସିଯିବ କି ବୋଲି ଆଶଙ୍କା ଜାଗେ।
entries.usage_example: One shop is penalised for unsafe wiring, and neighbouring owners anxiously inspect their own shops. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The first clause is elliptical in the captured wording. It is preserved without supplying a missing verb; the source gloss supports the shared-fear reading.

entries.title: Do not laugh at another’s turn
entries.odia:
ଉପର ବରଡ଼ା ଖସୁଛି,
ମଝି ବରଡ଼ା ହସୁଛି 
ତଳ ବରଡ଼ା କହୁଛି,
ମୋ ଦିନ କାଳ ଯାଉଛିରେ ଭାଇ ତୋ ଦିନକାଳ ଆସୁଛି ॥
entries.literal_meaning: The upper leaf falls; the middle leaf laughs; the lower leaf says, “My time is passing, brother; your time is coming.”
entries.explanation: The speaking leaves place laughter beside the passing of time. Read cautiously, the verse warns against treating another’s decline as something that can never reach oneself.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟର ଅବସ୍ଥା ବଦଳିବା ଦେଖି ହସିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ନିଜ ପାଳି କଥା ଭାବିବାକୁ ଏହା ମନେ ପକାଏ। ସମୟ କାହା ପାଇଁ ଅଟକି ରହେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Younger colleagues mock a retiring worker until they consider their own eventual retirement. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: No explanatory gloss accompanies this verse. The sequence of upper, middle and lower leaves is retained exactly; no botanical species, original voice or corrected sequence is asserted.

entries.title: The world keeps changing
entries.odia: ବେଙ୍ଗ କହେ ବେଙ୍ଗୁଲିଲୋ ପୃଥ୍ଵୀ ଘଡ଼ିକେ ଆନ ।
entries.literal_meaning: The frog tells the female frog: the world is different from one moment to the next.
entries.explanation: Circumstances do not remain as they were. The animal conversation makes a simple observation about change, without saying that every change is good or bad.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅବସ୍ଥା ସବୁବେଳେ ଏକ ରହେନାହିଁ। ବେଙ୍ଗ ଓ ବେଙ୍ଗୁଲିର କଥାରେ ପୃଥିବୀର ଏହି ବଦଳୁଥିବା ରୂପ ଧରାପଡ଼େ।
entries.usage_example: A familiar market has changed so much that a returning visitor must learn its new arrangements. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source explicitly glosses changing circumstances; the dialogue is not attached to a verified folktale here.

entries.title: Distance does not end a claim
entries.literal_meaning: Even in the forest, the elephant belongs to the king.
entries.explanation: The line presents a claim that persists despite distance. Applied figuratively, it can suggest that being out of sight does not by itself remove someone’s connection or responsibility.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୂରେ ରହିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ସମ୍ପର୍କ କିମ୍ବା ଦାବି ଶେଷ ହୁଏନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଏହି କଥାକୁ ବୁଝାଯାଇପାରେ। ଏହା ଏଠାରେ ଏକ ସୀମିତ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
entries.usage_example: Equipment lent to another office remains the lender’s responsibility to keep on its inventory. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: No source gloss accompanies the line. It is not used as evidence for any historical law giving a king ownership of all elephants.

entries.title: Help answered with an insult
entries.odia: ଉପକାର କଲି କୁକୁରକୁ କୁକୁର ମୁତିଲା ଉପରକୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: I helped the dog; the dog urinated upwards at me.
entries.explanation: The crude image expresses resentment when help is answered with harm or disrespect. It describes a feeling of betrayal, not a reason to assume everyone who needs help will be ungrateful.
entries.meaning_odia: ଉପକାରର ପ୍ରତିଦାନରେ ଅପମାନ କିମ୍ବା କ୍ଷତି ମିଳିଲେ ଯେଉଁ କ୍ଷୋଭ ଜାଗେ, ଏହି କଟୁ କଥା ତାହାକୁ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: After covering a colleague’s shift, someone discovers that the colleague has blamed them for a mistake. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source gives an ingratitude gloss. The bodily image is intentionally coarse and should not be presented as polite praise or animal-behaviour evidence.

entries.title: Devotion and an empty stomach
entries.odia:
ଠକ ଠକ ମାଳି ଭଜନ ଟାଣ
ଭୋକ କଲା ଭାତ ପାଖକୁ ଆଣ |
entries.literal_meaning: “Thaka thaka Mali, bhajana tana”; when hunger comes, bring the rice near. (The opening phrase is retained in transliteration because its precise literal force remains uncertain.)
entries.explanation: The verse sets a loud display of devotion beside an ordinary appetite. It can be read as a jab at performance that conceals self-interest, though the source gives no separate explanation.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜୋରରେ ଭଜନ ଗାଇବା ଓ ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଲେ ଭାତ ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ଏକାଠି ରଖି ଏହି ପଦ ଦେଖାଣିଆ ଭକ୍ତିକୁ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରୁଥିବା ଭଳି ଲାଗେ। ଏହା ଏକ ସୀମିତ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
entries.usage_example: A fictional character makes a grand show of sacrifice but promptly insists on a special meal. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: ମାଳି remains a source label, not a judgment about a caste or occupation. Neither hunger nor devotional singing is itself treated as proof of hypocrisy. The opening ଠକ ଠକ and ଭଜନ ଟାଣ are not given a definite literal gloss; the interpretation remains provisional.
